title: LESSViT: Robust Hyperspectral Representation Learning under Spectral Configuration Shift
claim: A model that handles varying input configurations combines a robust masked-pretraining pipeline with an efficient factorized attention module.
layout: 3 panels: left setting column, top pretraining flow, bottom attention detail
description: A three-panel composite figure with blue rounded borders. The left panel, 'Cross-Spectral Generalization', stacks a training sensor (Sensor A, in-distribution) above four evaluation sensors (B to D). Each sensor has a hyperspectral cube image, an icon and a colored spectral curve. A dashed line separates training from evaluation. The top-right panel shows the HyperMAE pretraining pipeline as a two-row loop of boxes and arrows. Input HSI goes through HCS ratio, tied patch embedding, decoupled spatial-spectral masking, the LESSViT encoder, and reconstruction with an L_MIM loss. Token grids appear at several stages. The bottom-right panel details LESS Attention and SSRoPE. It has a central block diagram with spectral and spatial attention branches, a green Spectral RoPE panel with rotation geometry and a wavelength bar, and an orange Spatial RoPE panel with rotation plots. Colors are teal-green remote-sensing imagery with blue, green and orange accents.
caption: Overview of LESSViT for cross-spectral generalization. \textcircled{ 1}: Cross-spectral generalization setting: train on a fixed spectral configuration and evaluate across spectral configurations with varying wavelength coverage and channel configurations. \textcircled{ 2}: HyperMAE pretraining with decoupled spatial–spectral masking and hierarchical channel sampling for scalable and robust learning. \textcircled{ 3}: LESS Attention with SSRoPE for efficient spatial–spectral modeling.
abstract: Modeling hyperspectral imagery (HSI) across different sensors presents a fundamental challenge due to variations in wavelength coverage, band sampling, and channel dimensionality. As a result, models trained under a fixed spectral configuration often fail to generalize to other sensors. Existing Vision Transformer (ViT) approaches either rely on implicit spectral modeling with fixed channel assumptions or adopt explicit spatial-spectral attention with prohibitive computational cost, leading to a fundamental trade-off between efficiency and expressiveness. In this work, we introduce Low-rank Efficient Spatial-Spectral ViT (LESSViT), a sensor-flexible architecture for cross-spectral generalization. LESSViT is built on LESS Attention, a structured low-rank factorization that models joint spatial-spectral interactions through separable spatial and spectral components, reducing the complexity of full spatial-spectral attention from $\mathcal{O}(N^2 C^2)$ to $\mathcal{O}(rNC)$, where $N$ is the number of spatial tokens, $C$ is the number of spectral channels, and $r$ is the rank of the low-rank approximation. We further incorporate channel-agnostic patch embedding and wavelength-aware positional encoding to support flexible spectral inputs. To enable efficient and robust pretraining, we introduce a hyperspectral masked autoencoder (HyperMAE) with decoupled spatial-spectral masking and hierarchical channel sampling. We evaluate LESSViT under a cross-spectral generalization setting that simulates cross-sensor variability. Experiments on the SpectralEarth benchmark demonstrate that LESSViT improves robustness under spectral shifts while remaining competitive in-distribution, and explicit and efficient spatial-spectral modeling is essential for scalable and generalizable hyperspectral representation learning. The code is available through the project page: https://uiuctml.github.io/LESSViT/
